documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46 y/o here for his yearly exam, rescheduled from April. Doing well. No flank pain or urinary trouble since the left stone passed last October. Says he is drinking more water at his desk than he used to, though not every day. No meds. NKDA.
Colonoscopy 6/2024 normal, due 2034. Tdap 2023.

ROS: negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, in no distress. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck without nodes or thyromegaly. RRR, no murmur. Clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Skin unremarkable. Extremities without edema.
PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment: well adult; history of one passed ureteral stone, quiet.
Plan: CBC, CMP, lipids. Keep fluids up. Fall vaccines. See him in a year.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal again this year, blood counts, kidney function, liver tests and cholesterol. Have a good summer.

conditions.label: Calculus of ureter
conditions.note: Right distal ureter, small, radiolucent on scout

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth once daily until the stone passes, up to 4 weeks
Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text:
Technique: noncontrast helical CT, abdomen and pelvis, stone protocol.
Comparison: CT 09/29/2024.
Findings: small calculus in the distal right ureter. The stone is not visible on the scout radiograph. No hydronephrosis. Left ureter now clear; the previously seen left ureteral stone is no longer present. Kidneys normal in size without parenchymal stones. Bladder decompressed, unremarkable. Bowel and appendix normal. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Small distal right ureteral calculus, radiolucent on scout, which can be seen with uric acid stones. No obstruction.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital ED. Encounter 10/12/2025 (Sunday). Copy to PCP.

Chief complaint: right flank pain.
History: 46M, about a year out from a left-sided stone seen here 9/2024. Woke at 4 am with sharp pain in the right flank that came on all at once and travels to the right groin. Nauseated, threw up twice, nothing bloody. No fall or injury. No fever, no burning, not urinating more than usual.
Diet: high protein, low carb for the last several months. Alcohol occasionally.
Allergies: none known. Home meds: none.

Exam: vitals WNL. Uncomfortable. R CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft without peritoneal signs.
UA: reddish-orange, clear; pH 5.0; small blood, 6-10 RBC/hpf, 0-2 WBC, nitrite/LE neg. Microscopy reviewed, no casts.
Labs: Ca 9.4, Cr 1.0; CBC unremarkable.
CT noncontrast: small stone, distal right ureter, not seen on scout (radiolucent), no hydro.

Treatment: ketorolac 15 mg IV, ondansetron 4 mg IV. Pain controlled, drinking without vomiting.

Dx: right ureterolithiasis; radiolucent stone, consider uric acid.
Plan: home. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily until passed, ondansetron ODT 4 mg q8h prn, ibuprofen with food. Strainer given, please save the stone for analysis. PCP follow-up within a week; return if fever or intractable pain.

documents.title: Pt passed stone
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Seen in ED Sunday for R ureteral stone. Passed it this morning into the strainer, small tan stone. Pain gone, no fever, keeping food down. Advised to keep it dry in a clean container and bring it to his visit Monday 10/20 with PCP. Ok to stop ondansetron, finish tamsulosin until seen. Pt verbalized understanding.

conditions.label: Personal history of urinary calculi
conditions.note: Left ureteral stone 9/2024, right ureteral stone 10/2025, both passed

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Recurrent Stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ED Sunday 10/12 with R renal colic, small distal R ureteral stone on CT, radiolucent on the scout. Ca 9.4, Cr 1.0 there. Passed it 10/14 into the strainer, brought it in today. No pain since. No fever, urine looks normal now. Stopped ondansetron, has a few tamsulosin left.
This is his second stone in about a year (left, 9/2024, passed, not caught). Father with stones. He has been on a high-protein, low-carb eating plan for a few months; fluids so-so.

O: afebrile, vitals fine. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen benign.

A/P:
1. R ureteral stone, passed. Stop tamsulosin. Resolved.
2. Recurrent nephrolithiasis, two stones in 13 months. Stone sent for analysis today. Radiolucent stone and acidic urine in the ED make uric acid likely, but we'll see. Referring to urology for a metabolic workup (24 h urine). Until then: aim for 2.5 L of urine a day, ease off the red meat and protein shakes.
3. Flu and COVID today.
Message when the stone analysis is back.

documents.title: Your stone analysis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Chris, the stone came back as pure uric acid. That type forms when urine runs acidic and concentrated, and a protein-heavy diet adds to it. The good part is that it usually responds well to making the urine less acidic plus more fluid. Urology has your referral and the result; they will go over the 24 hour urine with you.

documents.title: RE: Your stone analysis
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Urology called, I'm in December 9. Already cut back on the shakes.

medications.drug_text: potassium citrate 15 MEQ Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

conditions.label: Personal history of urinary calculi
conditions.note: Uric acid stones; on potassium citrate per urology

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Visit 12/09/2025.
Re: Christopher Sanborn, 46. Referred by primary care for recurrent stones.

Thank you for sending Mr. Sanborn. He has had two symptomatic ureteral stones, left in September 2024 (passed, not retrieved) and right in October 2025 (passed, retrieved; analysis 100% uric acid). The second was radiolucent on the CT scout. No gout. Father formed stones. Takes no medications; NKDA. Diet has leaned high protein and low carbohydrate this year, which he is already pulling back. Estimates 1.5 L of fluid a day.

Exam: well, no flank tenderness.

24-hour urine (collected 12/02): volume 1.4 L/day, pH 5.2, uric acid 690 mg/day, calcium 190 mg/day, citrate 540 mg/day. Serum uric acid 6.4 mg/dL.

Assessment: uric acid nephrolithiasis driven chiefly by low urine pH and low urine volume; urinary uric acid and calcium are not elevated, serum uric acid normal.

Plan:
1. Potassium citrate ER 15 mEq twice daily with meals. Check potassium and creatinine in a few months (happy for primary care to do this).
2. Fluids to make at least 2.5 L of urine per day.
3. Less animal protein.
4. Home urine pH dipsticks, target 6.0 to 6.5.
5. Repeat 24-hour urine and renal ultrasound in about 6 months, then see me.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pharmacy call re potassium citrate
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy called to confirm we are aware urology started potassium citrate ER 15 mEq BID; they only had 10 mEq tabs in stock and wanted to know whether to substitute. Told them to order the 15 mEq, pt agreed to wait a day. Added to med list per urology letter. No interacting meds.

documents.title: pH strips
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update. Been on the potassium citrate two months. Strips mostly read 6.0 to 6.5 now, first week they were down around 5.5. No stomach upset. Carrying a big water bottle everywhere. Anything else I should be doing?

documents.title: RE: pH strips
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is exactly the range urology wants, nice work. Keep going. When you come in for your physical in April we'll check your potassium and kidney numbers on the citrate.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, turns 47 this week.

Interval: urology 12/2025 for his two uric acid stones. 24 h urine showed acidic, low-volume urine; started potassium citrate ER 15 mEq BID. Tolerating it without GI upset. Home pH 6.0 to 6.5. Drinking much more, eating less meat, dropped the low-carb plan. No flank pain, no hematuria, no stone passage since October. Repeat 24 h urine and ultrasound with urology in June.
Meds: potassium citrate ER 15 mEq twice daily. NKDA.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2024 normal; Tdap 2023; flu and COVID last fall.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Pleasant, well. HEENT normal. No adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no CVA tenderness. Skin and extremities unremarkable.
PHQ-2 0.

Assessment and plan:
1. Personal history of uric acid stones, on potassium citrate. BMP today for potassium and creatinine. Continue as urology directs.
2. Health maintenance: lipids and CBC with today's draw.
Booked to see me in October with his flu shot.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium is 4.6, right where it should be on the citrate, and kidney function is normal. Cholesterol and blood counts normal too. No changes.

reports.text: Right kidney 11.2 cm, left kidney 11.0 cm, normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No calculi. No hydronephrosis on either side. Bladder unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Normal renal ultrasound. No calculi or hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Visit 06/16/2026.

Mr. Sanborn returns six months after starting potassium citrate for uric acid stones. No pain episodes or passed stones. Taking potassium citrate ER 15 mEq twice a day consistently; home strips 6.0 to 6.5. Primary care potassium in April was normal.

Repeat 24-hour urine: volume 2.3 L/day, pH 6.4.
Renal ultrasound 06/09: no stones, no hydronephrosis in either kidney.

Impression: uric acid nephrolithiasis, well controlled on alkalinization with improved urine volume.
Plan: continue potassium citrate and fluids. Return in 12 months with a renal ultrasound, sooner for symptoms.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the potassium citrate is out of refills from urology. Can you send a 90 day supply? Same pharmacy.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per your doctor, sent: potassium citrate ER 15 mEq, one twice daily, 180 tablets with 3 refills. We saw the June urology note; glad everything looked clear.
